name: TraumaCore
teaser: TraumaCore is a damage and armor overhaul for SPT that makes shot placement, bleeding, bones, and repeated armor hits more important. by adding more hitboxes and changing how damage works
description_html:
TraumaCore

TraumaCore is a damage and armor overhaul for SPT that makes shot placement, bleeding, bones, and repeated armor hits more important.

Warning: This mod makes combat significantly more hardcore. Every successful hit inflicts bleeding, and any well-placed shot has the potential to end your run.

TraumaCore fundamentally changes how combat works. Every hit now creates trauma and blood loss rather than simply subtracting health from a body part, making fights significantly more unforgiving. Bringing enough medical supplies to control bleeding is essential, as untreated wounds can continue draining blood long after the shooting stops. You may survive a heavy exchange, kill the enemy, and still collapse seconds later from the wounds you took during the fight.

Medical items and stims have also been rebalanced around this system. Using a stim that use to remove bleeds now clears all active TraumaCore bleeds and reduces further bleed damage by 50% for the duration of the stim, rather than simply removing existing bleeds like in vanilla EFT. Healing items have also been adjusted so treating a limb removes all bleed stacks currently affecting that limb.

Other mods approach this concept in different ways, but TraumaCore is my own take on it.

This replaces EFT’s traditional body-part health system with a blood-based damage model. Instead of bullets simply reducing a hitbox’s health pool, wounds drain from your total blood supply over time based on their severity. A chest shot may not kill immediately, but without treatment the resulting blood loss can become fatal seconds later. Hits can also damage vital structures such as the brain, heart, spine, and major bones, making shot placement matter far more than simply depleting a body part’s HP.

The default settings are balanced around player-vs-AI combat, with most of the new effects applying more heavily to AI while the player remains closer to a vanilla+ experience. Accurate shots to vital areas can end fights quickly, stacked chest wounds become increasingly dangerous, and shots to the arms or legs are less effective than center-mass hits. By default, players also use more forgiving organ settings than AI and Scavs.

Features

  • Blood-loss-based damage instead of traditional direct HP damage
  • Bruising and blunt trauma when armor stops incoming rounds
  • Spinal fractures from spinal trauma
  • Guaranteed fatal heart injuries and Potentially fatal internal bleeding
  • Rebalanced medical items and stims

Anatomical Hitboxes

  • Brain and lower-brain hitboxes that move with the head
  • A fatal cervical-spine hitbox through the neck
  • A lower spine running from the chest to the pelvis
  • A heart hitbox inside the chest
  • Major bones in the arms and legs

Brain and cervical-spine hits are fatal. Heart hits cause extremely fast bleeding. Lower-spine hits cause a spinal fracture, while hits to limb bones can fracture the affected arm or leg.

The hitboxes follow the character’s movement and animations. They do not make the entire head or chest count as an organ hit, the bullet must pass through the smaller internal area. this makes for more accurate gunplay but can make it feel more unforgiving as if you miss the brain and hit the face its not a instant kill

Wounds and Bleeding

Most bullet damage is converted into wounds instead of being applied immediately.

  • Chest wounds stack with repeated hits.
  • Heart wounds cause fast bleeding that cannot be treated normally.
  • Face, stomach, arm, and leg wounds bleed at different rates.
  • Ordinary bleeding becomes weaker after the last hit.
  • Blacked body parts pass some damage toward connected healthy parts.
  • Arms transfer less damage than legs or the stomach.

This makes center-mass hits reliable without making every chest shot an instant kill. Limb shots can still be lethal, but generally require more hits or time than vital-area damage.

Armor

Armor either stops a shot or allows it through based on the ammunition, armor class, material, condition, and covered area.

When armor stops a shot, that location becomes weakened. Repeated hits near the same point deal increasing armor damage, up to five times the normal durability loss. This does not guarantee penetration, but it prevents the same small area from behaving like untouched armor after several impacts.

Stopped rounds can also cause a temporary Bruised effect that reduces movement speed and stamina recovery.

Hit Feedback

  • Custom icons for Bruised, Heart Wound, and Spinal Fracture
  • Blood particles emitted from the wound location
  • A small amount of blood when shooting a recently killed body
  • Death and agony sounds for delayed bleed-out deaths
  • Optional hitbox and intersection renderer for testing

The debug renderer is disabled by default.

Default Balance

TraumaCore is enabled for players, AI, and scavs by default.

AI and scavs use the complete organ system. Players begin with brain and lower-spine hitboxes enabled, while player heart and cervical-spine hitboxes are disabled to reduce sudden deaths from AI fire.

Usage

Press F12 to open the BepInEx Configuration Manager and select TraumaCore.

The menu includes separate controls for player and AI hitboxes, bleeding, damage linkage, armor behavior, blood effects, logging, and effect-testing buttons.
